title: Scale-of-measurement property checklist
trigger: For any statement about a scale type, run the checklist: nominal = labels/categories only (no order); ordinal = ranked but gaps unequal/unmeasurable; interval = equal gaps but NO true zero, so ratios are meaningless (e.g. 40°C is not 'twice' 20°C); ratio = equal gaps AND a true zero, so ratios ARE meaningful (e.g. income, weight, age) — the presence/absence of a genuine zero point is what separates interval from ratio.

title: Descriptive vs inferential statistics scope
trigger: Ask of each statement: does it merely summarize/organize the data actually collected (mean, chart, table -> descriptive), or does it use a sample to draw a conclusion, estimate, or generalization about a larger population, typically invoking probability or hypothesis testing (-> inferential)? Statements that mention 'generalizing', 'population', 'sampling error', or 'testing a claim' are inferential; statements that just 'present' or 'summarize' data are descriptive.

title: Cross-sectional vs time-series vs data-type classification
trigger: First classify the collection structure: same variable(s) tracked over multiple time periods = time-series; different units/subjects observed at a single point in time = cross-sectional. Then classify each variable separately as qualitative (categorical, e.g. nominal/ordinal labels) or quantitative (numeric), and as structured (tabular/numeric) or unstructured (text, images, free-form) when that distinction is tested.

title: True/false statements on categorical variable properties
trigger: Classify the variable as nominal or ordinal, then recall that mode is a valid summary for categorical data while covariance/correlation require numeric (interval/ratio) variables — check each statement against these definitions rather than computing anything.

title: Convert pie chart percentages to actual amounts
trigger: Multiply each category's stated percentage by the known total (or back out the total from one category's percent-and-value pair), then add or subtract the resulting amounts as the question asks.

title: Evaluate statements from a pie chart of percentages
trigger: Work directly with the percentage shares shown (no total needed) — rank categories by their percent slice or sum two slices to check a claimed comparison, then judge each statement true/false.

title: Compute relative frequency from a bar chart
trigger: Read off the bar height (frequency) for the category asked about, sum all bar heights to get the total, and divide: relative frequency = category frequency / total frequency.

title: IQR via ordered data and quartile position formula
trigger: Sort the data, locate Q1 and Q3 using the quartile position formula (e.g. (n+1)/4 and 3(n+1)/4), then IQR = Q3 - Q1.

title: Combined/weighted mean of merged subgroups
trigger: Use Sum(x) = n * mean for the whole group and for each subgroup; since the whole group's total sum equals the sum of subgroup totals, solve the resulting linear equation for the missing subgroup total or single observation.

title: Solve for unknown(s) from a given mean, then derive another statistic
trigger: Set up Sum(x) = n * mean as an equation in the unknown(s) (an unknown data value, a misrecorded entry, or an unknown variance term), solve algebraically, then plug back to compute the requested derived quantity (corrected mean, median, or |difference of unknowns|).

title: Effect of a linear transform (y = a*x + b) on mean, median, percentile, variance, IQR
trigger: For y = a*x + b: mean_y = a*mean_x + b and var_y = a^2*var_x; any single-point location statistic (median, a percentile) transforms the same way as the mean (multiply by a, add b); spread measures based on differences of two points (like IQR) are unaffected by a pure shift (b) and scale by |a| under a scale change.

title: Compute Pearson r from raw paired data
trigger: Given paired (x,y) observations, compute r = [nΣxy - ΣxΣy] / sqrt([nΣx²-(Σx)²][nΣy²-(Σy)²]) (or use deviations from means) and read the sign/magnitude to judge strength and direction of the linear relationship.

title: Correlation invariance under linear transformation
trigger: If X and Y are each replaced by linear transforms a+bX and c+dY, correlation is unchanged in magnitude and its sign flips only if exactly one of b,d is negative — no recomputation needed, just track sign(b)*sign(d).

title: Read and reason from a contingency table
trigger: Locate the row/column intersection for the stated categories, use row/column/grand totals to back out any unknown cell via subtraction, then form the requested proportion (part/relevant total).

title: Multiplication rule: independent choices per slot
trigger: When a count is built from a sequence of independent slots/positions each with their own number of choices (grades per subject, digits per place with a restriction), multiply the number of choices for each slot together; for digit-restriction problems, count allowed digits per place separately (watch leading-digit restrictions) before multiplying.

title: Solve nPr/nCr equations and identities
trigger: When the problem gives an equation in nPr, nCr, or n! (e.g., nPr=42, n^n-n!=21) or asks which formula identity holds, write nPr=n!/(n-r)!, nCr=n!/(r!(n-r)!), and nCr=nPr/r!, then solve algebraically or test each identity directly by substitution.

title: Combinations with include/exclude/case-split constraints
trigger: When selecting a subgroup with 'at least one of X', 'must include X', 'must exclude X', or choosing from two separate pools (e.g. men and women), fix the required/excluded elements first and choose the rest with nCr, or split into disjoint cases and add the counts (addition principle).

title: Permutations of a word with repeated letters
trigger: Count the total letters n and the frequency of each repeated letter (p, q, r, ...), then divide n! by the product of the factorials of the repeat counts: n!/(p!q!r!...).

title: Rank of a word in dictionary order
trigger: Sort the word's distinct letters alphabetically; for each position (left to right) count how many still-unused letters smaller than the actual letter could go there, multiply that count by the permutations of the remaining letters (adjusting for repeats), sum these contributions across all positions, and add 1 for the word itself.

title: Arrangements with together/apart positional restrictions
trigger: For items that must stay together, glue them into a single block, permute the block internally, then permute the block along with the remaining items; for items that must NOT be adjacent, first arrange the unrestricted items, then place the restricted items into the gaps between them.

title: List sample space to identify favorable outcomes
trigger: When the experiment has a small finite number of outcomes (e.g. a family of 3 children, coin/die combos), write out the full sample space explicitly and count the outcomes matching the event condition rather than reaching for a formula.

title: Combinations for equally-likely counting probability
trigger: When a fixed-size sample is drawn from a group with subtypes (e.g. draw k items from a pool, or pick a team), compute P = C(favorable subgroup, chosen)/C(total, chosen), summing numerator terms if 'favorable' covers multiple disjoint subgroup splits (e.g. 'all same colour' = all-red + all-blue).

title: Addition rule for union of mutually exclusive/simple events
trigger: For 'P(A or B)' with categories that can't overlap (or overlap is given as zero), just add P(A)+P(B); recognize the cue words 'either...or' / listed disjoint categories as the trigger for direct addition, no subtraction term needed.

title: Solve for unknown probability using union equations
trigger: When given multiple P(X or Y) values sharing a common unknown category, write each as an addition-rule equation (P(A∪B)=P(A)+P(B) when exclusive, or use total-probability/complement identities), then solve the resulting system algebraically for the unknown term.

title: Joint probability from a two-way contingency table
trigger: When probabilities are organized in a table crossing two attributes (e.g. disease status x test result), read the single cell corresponding to the AND condition directly (or divide the relevant cell by the table total) rather than combining marginal probabilities.

title: Sequential/conditional probability of an outcome pattern
trigger: When the question describes a process that stops on a pattern (e.g. repeated tosses until two consecutive matches), enumerate the toss-by-toss sequences that satisfy the stopping condition at exactly the given step, multiplying per-step probabilities (independence) for each valid path and summing over paths.

title: Conditional probability directly from a PMF
trigger: When given P(X=x) values or a PMF, compute P(A|B) = P(A cap B)/P(B) by summing PMF values that satisfy both conditions and dividing by the sum of PMF values satisfying the given condition -- no Bayes formula needed, just the definition applied to the distribution.

title: Conditional probability from a two-way contingency table
trigger: When data is laid out as a two-way frequency/contingency table, restrict attention to the row or column matching the given condition, then divide the count (or probability) in the target cell by the row/column total -- read the answer straight off the table instead of building a probability tree.

title: Independent events: complement and at-least-one/exactly-one rules
trigger: Recognize independence lets you multiply marginal probabilities directly: use P(at least one occurs) = 1 - product of (1 - P(i)) for independent successes, and for 'exactly one happens / they contradict' outcomes sum P(A)(1-P(B)) + (1-P(A))P(B) -- never subtract an overlap term since events are independent, not disjoint.

title: Law of total probability and Bayes' theorem over a partition
trigger: Identify the partition of the sample space (boxes, coins, bags, student groups) with known prior probabilities and known conditional probabilities of the event within each branch; compute P(event) = sum of P(event|partition_i)*P(partition_i) via a probability tree, and for a posterior question ('given the event happened, probability it came from partition_i') divide P(event|partition_i)*P(partition_i) by that same total -- the total-probability sum IS the Bayes denominator.

title: Without-replacement draws: joint/conditional probability and independence (hypergeometric)
trigger: When items are drawn sequentially without replacement, multiply successive conditional probabilities while updating the counts after each draw (or use the hypergeometric formula C(k,x)*C(N-k,n-x)/C(N,n) for an exact count); to test independence, compute P(A cap B) this way and compare it to P(A)*P(B) -- without replacement they are almost never equal.

title: Support/range of a discrete RV from a counting setup
trigger: When a scenario describes drawing/selecting a fixed number of items from a population and asks only for the possible values of X (not probabilities), list the support as min = max(0, n_draws - non_favorable_count) up to max = min(n_draws, favorable_count).

title: PMF via combinatorial (hypergeometric-style) counting
trigger: When X counts favorable items drawn from a finite population (with or without replacement), compute P(X=k) as a ratio of combinations/counts of favorable-vs-total outcomes, e.g. C(favorable,k)*C(rest,n-k)/C(total,n), for each value in the support.

title: PMF of a sum via convolution over two independent trials
trigger: When X is the sum of two independent trial outcomes (e.g. two die throws), build the full joint outcome table and sum P(A=a)*P(B=b) over all pairs with a+b=x to get P(X=x).

title: Solve for an unknown constant via total-probability normalization
trigger: Whenever a PMF or CDF contains an unknown constant, use the fact that total probability equals 1 — sum all PMF terms to 1, or set the CDF value at the largest support point to 1 — and solve for the constant.

title: Extract a PMF value from the jump size of a step CDF
trigger: Given a step/piecewise CDF, recover P(X=x) as the size of the jump at x: F(x) minus F evaluated just below x.

title: Read cumulative/tail probability directly off a step CDF
trigger: Given a step CDF table or graph, read P(X<=a) directly as F(a), and get 'at least'/'greater than' probabilities as 1 - F(a) (or F just below a, for strict inequalities) with no extra computation.

title: Conditional probability computed from a CDF
trigger: For P(event1 | event2) from a CDF, compute P(event1 ∩ event2) and P(event2) separately as CDF-derived probabilities, then divide: P(A|B) = P(A∩B)/P(B).

title: Build a CDF from a PMF by cumulative summation
trigger: Given a PMF table, build the CDF by cumulatively summing PMF values up to and including each x: F(x) = sum of P(X=t) for all t <= x.

title: Conceptual true/false checks on discrete RVs and CDFs
trigger: For true/false statements about discrete RVs or CDFs, test each against the defining properties: CDF is non-decreasing, right-continuous, ranges 0 to 1; PMF values are non-negative and sum to 1; Bernoulli mean equals p — eliminate options that violate any property.

title: Direct expectation E(X) = sum x*p(x) from a PMF table
trigger: Given a PMF table (or one easily derived from a simple experiment like a sum of two throws), compute E(X) as the sum of each value times its probability, listing out the full table first.

title: Linearity of expectation for sums of indicator/count variables
trigger: Define X (and Y) as counts built from indicator variables over trials or selections, and use E(X+Y)=E(X)+E(Y): compute each simple marginal expectation separately even when X and Y are dependent, instead of building a joint distribution.

title: Expected number of trials in a without-replacement elimination process
trigger: Let X = the trial number on which success first occurs as items are removed without replacement; find P(X=k) by multiplying the chain of failure probabilities up to stage k-1 by the success probability at stage k, then sum k*P(X=k).

title: Back out an unknown PMF constant using a given E(X)
trigger: Write E(X)=sum x*p(x) in terms of the unknown constant(s), set it equal to the given expectation, and solve algebraically (pairing with Sum p(x)=1 as a second equation whenever there are two unknowns).

title: Expectation of a function g(X) via sum g(x)*p(x)
trigger: Never use the shortcut E[g(X)] = g(E[X]) for a nonlinear g; instead build a new row of g(x) values for every x in the PMF and sum g(x)*p(x) directly.

title: Linear transformation of expectation: E(aX+b) = aE(X)+b
trigger: Recognize the E(aX+b) shortcut: compute E(X) once from the PMF (solving for any unknown parameter via Sum p(x)=1 first if needed), then apply E(aX+b)=aE(X)+b instead of re-deriving from scratch.

title: Variance from a PMF: Var(X) = E(X^2) - [E(X)]^2
trigger: Compute E(X) and E(X^2) as two separate weighted sums from the PMF table, then apply Var(X)=E(X^2)-[E(X)]^2 — the standard two-step variance formula.

title: Variance with an unknown PMF parameter or a variance-property claim
trigger: Express p(x) in terms of the unknown parameter using Sum p(x)=1, then compute Var(X)=E(X^2)-[E(X)]^2 symbolically in that parameter; for true/false style claims, recall standard facts such as Var(Bernoulli)=p(1-p) and Var(constant)=0.

title: Variance under linear transformation and independent sums
trigger: Apply Var(aX+b)=a^2*Var(X), extending to Var(aX+bY)=a^2*Var(X)+b^2*Var(Y) when X and Y are independent — never let the additive constant b affect the variance.

title: Solve simultaneous E and Var equations for transformation constants
trigger: When told E(Y)=0 and Var(Y)=1 for Y=aX-b (or similar), write both E(aX-b)=aE(X)-b=0 and Var(aX-b)=a^2*Var(X)=1 as two equations in the unknowns and solve them simultaneously.

title: Binomial identification, PMF, and basic moments
trigger: Recognize a fixed number of independent trials with constant success probability p; use P(X=k)=C(n,k)p^k(1-p)^(n-k), E(X)=np, Var(X)=npq for exact-count, mean, or variance questions.

title: Binomial 'at most k' cumulative probability
trigger: For 'at most k' successes, sum the binomial PMF from 0 to k: P(X<=k) = sum_{i=0}^{k} C(n,i)p^i(1-p)^(n-i); with small k this is just adding a few terms.

title: Binomial 'at least k' via complement or direct sum
trigger: For 'at least k' successes, either sum PMF terms from k to n directly (few terms) or use the complement P(X>=k)=1-P(X<=k-1); for the special case k=1, use 1-(1-p)^n.

title: Conditional binomial probability given a restricted event
trigger: When asked for P(X=k | X>=1) note {X=k} is a subset of {X>=1} for k>=1, so the conditional probability simplifies to P(X=k)/P(X>=1); compute each piece with the binomial PMF/complement.

title: Recover binomial n and p from mean and variance
trigger: Given mean and variance of a binomial, set np=mean and npq=variance, divide to get q=variance/mean (so p=1-q), then solve n=mean/p; plug back into the PMF for the requested probability.

title: Shifted/transformed binomial random variable
trigger: For Y=X+c where X~Bin(n,p), the PMF just shifts support: P(Y=y)=P(X=y-c)=C(n,y-c)p^(y-c)(1-p)^(n-y+c); identify the new support range and match coefficients.

title: Poisson parameter recovery from a PMF ratio equation
trigger: When given an equation relating P(X=k) terms (e.g. aP(X=j)=bP(X=i)+cP(X=h)), write each term as e^-lambda*lambda^k/k!, cancel the common e^-lambda factor, and solve the resulting polynomial in lambda; if asked for E(X^2), use E(X^2)=lambda+lambda^2 and Var(X)=lambda=SD^2.

title: Poisson cumulative and ratio-of-cumulative probability
trigger: For 'at most k' or ratios of cumulative Poisson probabilities, compute each P(X=i)=e^-lambda*lambda^i/i! for i=0..k and sum (or take the ratio of two partial sums) directly.

title: Poisson rate scaling to a different time/space interval
trigger: When the given rate is per one interval but the question asks about a different-length interval, first rescale lambda proportionally (lambda_new = lambda_given * (interval_new/interval_given)), then apply the Poisson PMF or complement as needed.

title: Poisson moments and linear combinations of independent Poissons
trigger: For independent Poisson variables, Var(X)=E(X)=lambda and SD=sqrt(lambda); for a linear combination Var(aX+bY)=a^2*Var(X)+b^2*Var(Y) since independence gives zero covariance, so solve for the unknown mean/rate algebraically.

title: Point probability is zero for continuous RV
trigger: For any continuous distribution, P(X = k) = 0 for a single exact value since it's the area of a single vertical line under a density curve; recognize 'probability of exactly ___' questions and answer 0 without computing anything.

title: Uniform distribution: mean and median by direct formula
trigger: Recall directly that mean = median = (a+b)/2 for Uniform(a,b); just plug in the given endpoints, no integration or interval-ratio needed.

title: Uniform distribution: interval/tail/percentile probability via length ratio
trigger: For Uniform(a,b), P(x1<X<x2) = (x2-x1)/(b-a); use this same ratio equation to compute a probability, or to solve for an unknown bound x1/x2 (or a percentile point) by isolating the unknown in the equation.

title: Uniform distribution: solving for endpoints from mean/variance
trigger: Set up E(X)=(a+b)/2 and/or Var(X)=(b-a)^2/12 as equations in the unknown endpoint(s), then solve the resulting linear (or simultaneous) system algebraically; if a further probability is asked, plug the recovered a,b into the interval-ratio formula.

title: Uniform distribution: conditional probability on a truncated interval
trigger: For Uniform(a,b), given X>c the conditional distribution is Uniform(c,b); so P(X>d | X>c) = (b-d)/(b-c) — rebuild the ratio using the truncated interval (c,b), not the original (a,b).

title: Exponential distribution: CDF/tail probability from the mean
trigger: For Exponential with mean m (lambda=1/m), use P(X>t)=e^{-t/m} and P(X<t)=1-e^{-t/m}; for an interval, P(t1<X<t2)=e^{-t1/m}-e^{-t2/m}.

title: Exponential distribution: memoryless property
trigger: Recognize 'given it has already lasted s, find the probability it lasts t more' as memoryless: P(X>s+t | X>s) = P(X>t) = e^{-t/m} — drop the elapsed time s and treat the remaining wait as a fresh exponential.

title: Exponential distribution: inverting the CDF for time or parameter
trigger: When given a probability and asked for a time (or a probability condition used to pin down lambda/mean), set 1-e^{-t/m}=p (or use the median condition P(X<=x0)=P(X>x0)=0.5) and solve algebraically using logarithms for the unknown.

title: Exponential distribution: verify true/false statements (mean, variance, CDF)
trigger: Check each candidate statement independently against the three core exponential facts: mean=1/lambda, variance=1/lambda^2, and CDF F(x)=1-e^{-lambda x} — evaluate statement-by-statement rather than reasoning about the distribution as a whole.

title: Normal distribution: symmetry and z-standardization statements
trigger: Use symmetry of the normal curve about mu (so P(X>mu)=P(X<mu)=0.5) and the standardization z=(x-mu)/sigma to test each statement, instead of computing a full integral for each one.

title: Normal distribution: recover a value from a percentile via z-score
trigger: To find c such that P(X < mu + c) = p, look up (or recall) the standard normal z-value corresponding to percentile p, then compute c = z*sigma.
